title: Whose number is greater in the ten second game?
description: Two players have ten seconds to write the larger number. In the first round one followed by thirteen zeroes meets nine hundred ninety nine thousand nine hundred ninety nine times itself, and in the second round four copies of ten to the power one thousand meet ten to the power one million times nine thousand. Each number is placed near a power of ten, and the bigger power decides.
teaching_notes: One idea: to compare huge numbers, place each near a power of ten, and the bigger power decides. Watch for students who are fooled by the long string of nines or by the factor nine thousand.

video_script.why: Huge numbers are compared by placing each near a power of ten. The bigger power of ten decides the round.
video_script.substitution: Write each number near a power of ten and compare the powers; check by counting digits.
video_script.anchor: a ten second game with two rounds of huge numbers
video_script.payoff_line: The bigger power of ten decides the round

final_answer.value: Round 1: the number written by {{NAME_2}}; Round 2: the number written by {{NAME_1}}
final_answer.spoken: In the first round, the number written by {{NAME_2}} is greater. In the second round, the number written by {{NAME_1}} is greater.

names.{{NAME_1}}: the child who writes the multiplication in the first round and ten to the power one million times nine thousand in the second
names.{{NAME_2}}: the child who writes one followed by thirteen zeroes and the four added copies

maths_rules: check by digits: 10¹³ has 14 digits, a number below 10¹² has at most 12; 4 × 10¹⁰⁰⁰ has 1001 digits, the other has 1000004
video_script.design: The two rounds sit in two columns. Each number is placed on a power-of-ten scale. The digit counts come in the last step.

beats.on_screen: Given: round 1: 10000000000000 and 999999 × 999999; round 2: 10¹⁰⁰⁰ added four times and 10¹⁰⁰⁰⁰⁰⁰ × 9000

beats.on_screen: To find: the greater number in each round

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the greater number in each round.

marks.s1: 10000000000000 is written with its 13 zeroes counted

narration: <bookmark mark='s1'/>Step one, the first round. The number written by {{NAME_2}} is one followed by thirteen zeroes.
<bookmark mark='p13'/>That is ten to the power thirteen.

marks.s2: 999999 is placed just before 10⁶ on a short scale

narration: <bookmark mark='s2'/>Step two, look at the number written by {{NAME_1}}.
<bookmark mark='six'/>Nine hundred ninety nine thousand nine hundred ninety nine is less than ten to the power six.
<bookmark mark='sq'/>Times itself, it is less than ten to the power six times ten to the power six.
<bookmark mark='p12'/>That is ten to the power twelve.

marks.s3: the second round is written with {{NAME_2}} beside the four added copies
marks.four: the four copies are grouped as 4 × 10¹⁰⁰⁰

narration: <bookmark mark='s3'/>Step three, the second round.
<bookmark mark='four'/>{{NAME_2}} added four copies of ten to the power one thousand.
That is four times ten to the power one thousand.

marks.mil: the words at least 10¹⁰⁰⁰⁰⁰⁰ appear under it

narration: <bookmark mark='s4'/>Step four, {{NAME_1}} wrote ten to the power one million, times nine thousand.
<bookmark mark='mil'/>This number is at least ten to the power one million.

beats.on_screen: check by counting digits: 10¹³ has 14 digits, below 10¹² at most 12 digits; 4 × 10¹⁰⁰⁰ has 1001 digits, the other has about a million

marks.s5: the digit counts 14 and at most 12 appear for the first round
marks.dig2: the digit counts 1001 and about a million appear for the second round

narration: <bookmark mark='s5'/>Step five, check by counting digits.
One followed by thirteen zeroes has fourteen digits.
A number below ten to the power twelve has at most twelve digits.
<bookmark mark='dig2'/>Four times ten to the power one thousand has about one thousand digits.
The other number in the second round has about one million digits.
